findings.title: Sitemap lastmod dates are missing or unreliable
findings.root_cause: Sitemap lastmod dates are missing, malformed or not set per page, so crawlers cannot rely on them to recrawl changed pages first

evidence.description: 200 of 200 valid lastmod values are the same date (2026-10-12), so they reflect when the sitemap was generated, not when each page changed

findings.evidence_text: 200 of 200 valid lastmod values are the same date (2026-10-12), so they reflect when the sitemap was generated, not when each page changed

suggested_action.summary: Publish an accurate <lastmod> for every sitemap URL
steps: Set lastmod from the date each page's content last changed, not the build time
Use W3C Datetime, for example 2026-03-01 or 2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Search and AI crawlers recrawl updated pages sooner and keep trusting the dates
suggested_action.verification: Re-run the audit and compare lastmod values with real content changes
suggested_action.implementation_detail: Set each sitemap lastmod from the date the page content last changed, in W3C Datetime form, never the build time and never a future date.
suggested_action.expected_outcome: Crawlers can rely on sitemap lastmod to find and recrawl pages that actually changed.
suggested_action.quadrant_label: Fill-in: small value, small work; do when convenient

findings.mechanism: Crawlers use sitemap lastmod to decide what to recrawl only while it is present and accurate; missing, invalid or build-stamped values are ignored, so updates are found late.
findings.implementation_detail: Set each sitemap lastmod from the date the page content last changed, in W3C Datetime form, never the build time and never a future date.

limitations: 301 discovered URL(s) were never fetched (permission, acquisition failure, or budget constraints; out of 307 discovered); findings reflect only the 6 page(s) actually crawled, not the whole site. The sample reached 2 of 6 site sections (first path segment).

Headless browser rendering was not available in this environment; rendering-gap findings are based on a static-content heuristic only and are reported as suspected/insufficient_evidence rather than confirmed.
No external search provider was configured; claim corroboration and off-site footprint assessment were not checked this run (not the same as "nothing found").

No search for same-named knowledge-graph entities was run: robots.txt for Wikidata and Wikipedia disallows their search endpoints, so only the agent stage (AG-05) can look the brand name up; namesake ambiguity is unassessed.
Linked sameAs and review profiles were not fetched (OFF_SITE_LOOKUP=0), so whether they resolve and belong to the brand was not checked.

Review and directory platforms (Trustpilot, G2, Google Business Profile and others) were not searched for the brand: they block automated clients, no search provider was configured, and the agent stage (AG-06) was not supplied. Only profiles linked from the site were considered.
Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP) were not measured: the audit runs no browser and no PAGESPEED_API_KEY is configured. Web-vitals findings are estimates from markup patterns, not measurements.
3 link(s) listed in llms.txt were not checked (another domain, robots rules, the per-audit cap or a fetch error; see coverage.llms_txt).
Colour contrast and tap-target size were judged only where inline styles set them; colours and sizes from stylesheets need a browser to compute and were not assessed.
37 same-origin content image(s) were not measured for file size (per-audit cap of 4 or remaining budget); cross-origin images are never requested, so their weight is unassessed.

confidence.method: min(sample_representativeness, observation_completeness, execution_penalty), where sample_representativeness = max(crawl_completeness, min(section_coverage, sample_size)), capped at 0.9 unless discovery_reliable is true, and crawl_completeness = pages_analyzed / pages_discovered; observation_completeness = (pages read in full + half of pages read in part) / (pages analyzed + challenged, waiting-room, timed-out and failed fetches). A weak link caps the score rather than being averaged out. identity_confidence is reported beside the score, not in it: it gates only the checks that depend on the brand's identity
confidence.interpretation: A heuristic rating of how far the report speaks for the whole site, not a calibrated probability. Each finding states its own confidence.

reasons.sample_representativeness: The page sample is small or one-sided: the crawl analyzed 5 of 307 discovered page(s) and reached 2 of 6 site section(s); the crawl is known to have missed URLs (a crawl or sitemap read limit, or URLs left unfetched).
reasons.observation_completeness: Every page the audit tried to read was read in full.
reasons.identity_confidence: The brand identity is clear: the Organization markup names one brand.

confidence.explanation: Confidence is low (0.17). The weakest of its parts sets the score, here the page sample. The page sample is small or one-sided: the crawl analyzed 5 of 307 discovered page(s) and reached 2 of 6 site section(s); the crawl is known to have missed URLs (a crawl or sitemap read limit, or URLs left unfetched). Brand identity (reported separately, not part of the score): The brand identity is clear: the Organization markup names one brand. The score rates how far the report speaks for the whole site; each finding has its own confidence and status, and a problem seen on a page is still real on that page.
